items.title: The comparison between the derived tensor product with the powers of an ideal and the ordinary products is a pro-isomorphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a Noetherian ring A, an ideal I and a bounded complex M of finite modules, the inverse system of comparison maps from the derived tensor product of I^n with M to the ordinary products I^n M is an isomorphism of pro-objects of the derived category (statement lines 29676-29685). The proof is a chain of three reductions, each of which has to be justified: the passage from the powers of the ideal to the system generated by finitely many chosen generators, the passage from an isomorphism of pro-objects of complexes to pro-isomorphisms on cohomology in each degree, and the replacement of M by a bounded above complex of finite free modules; only then does the Artin-Rees consequence apply (proof lines 29687-29733). The degree bound on the two systems, which comes from the number of generators, is what makes the second reduction legitimate. The counted span refers three times to results of this chapter, one of them after the reduction, all carried as navigation stubs.
